name: Memberful
tagline: Memberships, subscriptions, gated content, and WordPress integration

pricing.basis: monthly platform plan plus transaction fee
pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Build / Test
tiers.limits: Unlimited test duration, members and staff; 0 live paid transactions until launch.
tiers.notes: For building/testing only, not a production free plan.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: Unlimited members and staff; 4.9% Memberful transaction fee.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom scale, migration and support; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Build/Test mode is free with unlimited test members and staff, but live paid transactions are disabled; no production free tier
pricing.hiddenCosts: Standard adds a 4.9% Memberful transaction fee to Stripe payment-processing fees.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Memberful's durable value is payments, network, compliance, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a narrow membership infrastructure storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Stripe account and API keys in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations
whyPeopleStillPay: Memberful: Creators pay to outsource payments, tax complexity, disputes, deliverability, moderation, and the trust needed to convert strangers.
ongoingBurden: Own payments, webhooks, refunds, tax records, fraud, access control, file delivery, moderation, backups, and support.

alternatives.name: Ghost
alternatives.desc: Memberships, subscriptions and gated posts without a plugin pile; the whole site becomes a Ghost site.

facts.install: Run Ghost-CLI on supported Ubuntu/MySQL hosting; the official Docker path is available but still documented as preview
facts.dataFormat: Posts, members and settings in MySQL; images under Ghost's content directory by default or through a configured storage adapter
facts.gapVsPaid: Ghost replaces the whole publication rather than acting as a neutral membership layer on an existing WordPress site.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a server, domain, DNS, TLS and transactional/newsletter mail, plus Ghost upgrades

alternatives.name: Paid Memberships Pro
alternatives.desc: A WordPress membership paywall with recurring Stripe and PayPal billing; free software, paid in plugin upkeep.

facts.install: Install the WordPress plugin, create membership levels/pages, then connect a supported payment gateway
facts.dataFormat: WordPress users/usermeta plus PMPro membership, order and discount tables; card credentials remain with the payment gateway
facts.gapVsPaid: Paid Memberships Pro adds WordPress, plugin, gateway, webhook and server upkeep that Memberful manages as a service.
facts.setupBlocker: A maintained WordPress/HTTPS site, payment gateway, webhooks and reliable email delivery are prerequisites

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: A hosted membership site with recurring billing and 2,000 contacts free; WordPress integration is not the point.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, funnels, course/community content, orders, emails and uploaded files in systeme.io's vendor-managed cloud; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: systeme.io is not a clean WordPress membership layer; replacing Memberful means moving the membership experience into its funnel ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: Selling requires connecting a payment gateway; the free plan is capped at 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, one community and one custom domain

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A commerce backend is not a WordPress membership and gated-content product.

notes: Credibility row: Memberful survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Memberful; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + Stripe.
Primary job: Build a narrow membership infrastructure storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: fulfilment, email, and affiliate ecosystems; marketplace discovery and buyer trust; tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
